passage: Mentor's note, Tuesday. Siddharth (Class 12) printed a topper's daily routine of sixteen hours from social media and pinned it above his desk. It began before dawn and ran until midnight, with almost no room for meals. He kept it for ten days. By day eight he was late to class; on day ten he slept through the morning and told me he had not opened a book since. He now studies perhaps an hour a day. The schedule had no place for his sleep, his slower pace in chemistry or the fact that he needs a break after lunch. I asked him to note when he naturally gets sleepy and how long he can focus before his mind drifts. We meet again on Thursday. — Ishita

qa.q: How many hours did the copied schedule contain?
What might Siddharth be feeling now?
qa.a: Discouraged and drained: after the burnout he has almost stopped studying.

qa.q: What could Siddharth do instead of copying a schedule, and why?
qa.a: Build a timetable from his own sleep, focus span and pace, since a routine that ignores these breaks quickly.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Ishita?
qa.a: Ishita sees a student who worked hard on something unsuited to him and lost a lot, and wants to help him find his own rhythm instead of scolding.

grounding: A student copies a topper's sixteen-hour timetable from social media, burns out in ten days and nearly stops studying.

passage:
Monday

Day ten of the Topper Timetable, and I think I'm done.

Arohi sent me a post from a rank-holder: 5 am wake-up, sixteen hours of study, fifteen-minute meals, sleep at 11. He cleared the exam with a top rank, so I copied it exactly. Printed it and stuck it above my desk.

Days one to three: exhausted but proud. Day four: fell asleep at my desk at 2 pm. Day six: headache all day, snapped at Amma. Day eight: sat in front of physics and read one page for an hour.

Today I didn't study at all. I lay on the bed and scrolled. I feel worse than before I started, when I was doing seven solid hours.

That topper probably sleeps well and reads fast. I'm not him. I'm Mohit, and I need a timetable that fits me, not a screenshot.

qa.q: How many hours of study did the topper's timetable include?
How does Mohit feel on day ten?
qa.a: Mohit feels exhausted and defeated, worse than before the timetable, and a little angry with himself.

qa.q: What approach would suit Mohit better?
qa.a: Going back to around seven solid hours and building up slowly, with enough sleep, so the plan fits Mohit's own pace.

qa.q: How might Amma see the ten days?
qa.a: Amma probably felt worried and hurt, watching Mohit grow tired and snappy.

grounding: A diary shows a student adopting a rank-holder's sixteen-hour schedule from social media, burning out in ten days and dropping to almost no study.
